question:
**Identify the part of the sentence in which there is an error.**

Two-thirds (a)/ of the city (b)/ has been damaged (c)/ by the earthquake (d)
solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. no error .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence follows the rules of **Subject-Verb Agreement** regarding fractions and percentages.
 
• When a **fraction** (like Two-thirds) is followed by "of," the verb agrees with the **noun** that follows "of" (the object of the preposition).
 
• In this case, the noun is **"the city"**, which is a **singular countable noun**. Therefore, the singular auxiliary verb **"has"** is grammatically correct.
 
• The fraction **"Two-thirds"** is also correctly pluralized because the numerator (Two) is greater than one.

Correct sentence: *Two-thirds of the city has been damaged by the earthquake.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fractions with Plural Nouns:**

 
 
• **Rule:** If the noun following "of" is plural, use a plural verb.
 
• **Example:** Two-thirds of the **buildings have** been damaged.
 
 
 
• **Fractions with Uncountable Nouns:**
 
 
• **Rule:** If the noun following "of" is uncountable, use a singular verb.
 
• **Example:** Two-thirds of the **water has** been contaminated.
 
 
 
• **Hyphenation:** In formal writing, fractions used as nouns or adjectives (like two-thirds) are usually hyphenated.
